parts.text:
2
The diagram shows two vectors X and Y. The vectors are perpendicular to one another.
Y = 6.0 N
X = 8.0 N
What is the magnitude and direction of vector (X – Y)?
A
10.0 N at an angle of 37° downwards from the direction of X
B
10.0 N at an angle of 37° upwards from the direction of X
C
14.0 N at an angle of 53° downwards from the direction of X
D
14.0 N at an angle of 53° upwards from the direction of X

hints: Notice that $X = 8.0\text{ N}$ points to the right and $Y = 6.0\text{ N}$ points downwards, and the question asks for the vector combination $X - Y$.
Remember that subtracting $Y$ is the same as adding $-Y$, so reverse the $6.0\text{ N}$ arrow to point upwards while $X$ stays to the right.
Use Pythagoras for the $6$-$8$-$10$ right-angled triangle and $\tan\theta = 6.0/8.0$ to find the angle of the resultant above the line of $X$.
walkthrough: Identify the given vectors: $X = 8.0\text{ N}$ to the right and $Y = 6.0\text{ N}$ downwards, with the vectors perpendicular.
Rewrite the subtraction as addition of the reversed vector: $X - Y = X + (-Y)$, so $-Y$ is $6.0\text{ N}$ upwards.
Draw $X$ to the right with $-Y$ upwards tail-to-head. The resultant is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with legs $8.0\text{ N}$ and $6.0\text{ N}$.
Calculate direction from $X$ using tangent: $\tan\theta = 6.0/8.0 = 0.75$, so $\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.75) = 37^{\circ}$ upwards from the direction of $X$ because the vertical component is upwards.

A.explanation: The magnitude $10.0\text{ N}$ is correct but downwards is wrong because subtracting the $6.0\text{ N}$ downwards vector adds an upwards component.

B.explanation: Resultant magnitude is $\sqrt{8.0^2+6.0^2}=10.0\text{ N}$ and the $6.0\text{ N}$ reversed component points upwards from X at $\tan^{-1}(6.0/8.0)=37^{\circ}$.

C.explanation: $14.0\text{ N}$ is the scalar sum $8.0+6.0$, not the vector magnitude from Pythagoras, and the direction is also reversed.

D.explanation: $14.0\text{ N}$ incorrectly adds the magnitudes as scalars instead of using $R^2 = X^2+Y^2$ for perpendicular vectors.
